sections.title: SURVEY BASIS
sections.body:
**Archive interval:** Six evening passes completed during two dry-weather field periods

**Instrumentation:** Calibrated long-wave infrared radiometer, contact thermistors, portable weather station, and survey control targets

**Study boundary:** Exterior masonry and immediately adjacent exposed ground within the assigned sector; no interior access was included.

sections.title: OBSERVED VARIANCE
sections.body:
**Thermal response:** A compact central surface region reached the expected daytime peak but returned heat more slowly than the comparison surfaces after local sunset.

**Phase residual:** Corrected cooling curves retained an 18-to-26-minute lag across four of six passes. The residual did not track measured wind direction, surface shade, or contact-temperature error.

**Energy balance:** On two passes, integrated outward heat flux exceeded the upper modeled daytime absorption value by 5.8 and 6.4 percent after the stated emissivity and weather uncertainty was applied.

**Spatial form:** The strongest response remained inside the same projected surface boundary and weakened smoothly toward the outer faces.

sections.title: INTERPRETIVE LIMITS
sections.body:
**Ordinary explanations retained:** Unmapped void space, differing stone density, repair material, and surface-emissivity error remain viable explanations for the cooling lag.

**Unresolved point:** Those explanations did not reproduce the positive energy residual or its stable surface boundary. No source was identified, and the available measurements do not establish a hazardous condition.

sections.title: DISPOSITION
sections.body:
**Finding:** Reproducible positive thermal residual within a stable surface boundary; source and transfer mechanism unassigned

**Action:** Retain passive comparison data and repeat with an independent radiometer and subsurface density profile when access permits.

**Field restriction:** No intrusive sampling authorized under this record.

sections.title: COORDINATE & ACCESS SCHEDULE
sections.summary: Location references and third-party access documentation remain with the controlling office.
